item.text: I’ll first read the service documentation, then query the API with retry/token-refresh handling and verify the final JSON invariants before writing the sole deliverable.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The docs confirm 50-item pagination, short-lived bearer tokens, and per-customer discount records. I’m now walking every successful page, deduplicating globally by order ID, and caching customer lookups; UTC filtering and per-order half-up rounding are being applied locally.

item.command: /bin/bash -c "node -e \"\\nconst base='http://localhost:8080';\\nlet token=[REDACTED_SECRET] sleep=ms=>new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,ms));\\nasync function newToken(){const r=await fetch(base+'/token',{method:'POST'});if("'!r.ok)throw new Error('"'token '+r.status+' '+await r.text());token=(await r.json()).token;}\\nasync function get(path){\\n for(let tries=0;;tries++){\\n  if("'!token) await newToken();'"\\n  let r; try{r=await fetch(base+path,{headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+token}})}catch(e){if(tries>=20)throw e;await sleep(Math.min(1000*(tries+1),5000));continue}\\n  if(r.status===401){token=[REDACTED_SECRET]  if(r.status===429){let raw=r.headers.get('retry-after'),ms=1000;if(raw){let n=Number(raw);ms=Number.isFinite(n)?Math.ceil(n*1000):Math.max(0,Date.parse(raw)-Date.now())}else{try{let j=await r.json();ms=Math.ceil(1000*Number(j.retry_after||j.retry_after_seconds||1))}catch{}}await sleep(ms+25);continue}\\n  if(r.status>=500){if(tries>=20)throw new Error(path+' repeated '+r.status);await sleep(Math.min(500*(tries+1),5000));continue}\\n  if("'!r.ok)throw new Error(path+'"' '+r.status+' '+await r.text());return r.json();\\n }\\n}\\n(async()=>{\\nconst start=Date.parse('2025-03-01T00:00:00Z'),end=Date.parse('2025-06-01T00:00:00Z');\\nconst seen=new Set(),customers=new Map(),by={north:0,south:0,east:0,west:0};let duplicates=0,count=0,total=0,pages=0;\\nasync function customer(id){if("'!customers.has(id))customers.set(id,get('"'/customers/'+encodeURIComponent(id)));return customers.get(id)}\\nlet path='/orders?page=1';\\nwhile(path){const data=await get(path);pages++;for(const o of data.items){if(seen.has(o.id)){duplicates++;continue}seen.add(o.id);const t=Date.parse(o.placed_at);if(o.status"'!=='"'shipped'||"'!(t>=start&&t<end))continue;const c=await customer(o.customer_id);if(!(c.region in by))throw new Error('"'bad region '+c.region);const amount=Math.floor((o.amount_cents*(100-c.discount_pct)+50)/100);by[c.region]+=amount;total+=amount;count++}path=data.next}\\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify({result:{total_cents:total,order_count:count,duplicates_skipped:duplicates,by_region:by},meta:{pages,uniqueListings:seen.size,customers:customers.size}},null,2));\\n})().catch(e=>{console.error(e);process.exit(1)});\\n\""

item.text: The first in-memory runner hit a shell-quoting issue before making API requests; no data was processed or written. I’m correcting the runner and continuing with the same calculation and validation criteria.

The complete traversal returned 30 pages and found 20 repeated order listings. I have the candidate result; I’m doing an independent second pass and then will write and schema-check `result.json` while removing the temporary runner.
